verdict.rationale: LangSmith dashboards can group data by run tag or metadata to split it over application-specific attributes, and the platform tracks token usage and cost as metrics. However, the evidence never explicitly shows cost or token charts broken down per user, session, or feature via metadata. A community comment says capturing which user is involved takes extra work; that is an effort concern, not a concrete failure, so it does not make the claim disputed. Missing for 10: explicit docs that cost/token metrics can be grouped by custom metadata, documented per-user and per-session attribution workflow, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can attribute cost and usage to users, sessions, and features via custom metadata

citations.quote: You can use group by run tag or metadata to split data over attributes that are important to your application.
Prebuilt dashboards are created automatically for each project and cover essential metrics, such as trace count, error rates, token usage, and more.
LangSmith provides threshold-based alerting on the following metrics: Run Count, Cost, Errors, Feedback Score, Latency
